description: Major-version dependency upgrade across a monorepo: breaking API changes, lockfile conflicts, deprecation warnings and the services that pin the old version.

facts.statement: After major-upgrading the core dependency across the independently released monorepo services, the full CI run took 47 minutes.
The rollback commit for the `@acme/http-client` 2.x upgrade, applied before releasing `services/search-api`, had the commit hash prefix `a41b73f`.

During the core-dependency upgrade codemod, the function that aborts if an independently released service has not also been major-bumped is `assertServiceVersionCompatibility()` in `packages/upgrade/lib/check.ts`.
In the monorepo upgrade pipeline, each independently released service reads the v3 canary rollout percentage from the environment variable CORE_UPGRADE_V3_PERCENT.
During the major-version upgrade of the core dependency across the monorepo's independently released services, the shared publish workflow logged a retry setting of 3 publish retries.
The dependency-upgrade CLI requires `--allow-major-peer-versions` when a monorepo's independently released services update a core dependency across major versions.
During the major core-dependency upgrade rollout, the billing service writes upgrade-notice artifacts to the `billing-upgrade-notices-prod` S3 bucket.
The upgrade session notes that the first independently released service was pinned to core 4.0.0 at the seven-character commit prefix a7f3c12.
The upgrade script defined `bumpCoreMajor` to bump each independently released service's core dependency to the new major version.
Before publishing any independently released service after the core dependency major upgrade, the release gate must call `validateCoreMajorReleaseGraph`.
During the major upgrade of the core dependency, the shared monorepo tool invoked the method migrateDependentServiceLockfiles to update each independently released service's lockfile.
During the monorepo dependency upgrade review, the breaking version bump for the payments service was traced to commit hash prefix a7f3c9d.

messages.text: Upgrade the core dependency across the monorepo and keep every service building.

Yes, upgrade core from 3.x to 4.0.0 in packages/core/package.json and services/*/package.json. Keep Node 18, set CORE_MIGRATION=strict in .env.test. Run yarn workspaces foreach -A topological run test and node scripts/verify-lockfile.js. Do not bump service versions unless package.json changed.

The last tool output implies the upgrade surface is not limited to the root lockfile; it is a monorepo dependency graph with several independent release boundaries. Hits in packages/core-client/package.json:12 pinning core-sdk@4.7.2 and services/billing/package.json:18 pinning core-sdk@4.6.0 mean at least two independently released services still depend on different majors. The pnpm-workspace.yaml:3 glob and turbo.json:9 remote caching flag suggest downstream builds can mask version drift if cached artifacts are reused. The error in services/inventory/src/legacyAdapter.ts:84 that createClient is missing the required transport property is expected for the 5.x breaking API, but its early appearance before typecheck of services/billing indicates the migration is not purely mechanical: old callers assume synchronous client creation while 5.x requires an explicit transport. The root pnpm-lock.yaml update alone is insufficient; each release package’s semver contract and consumer call sites need inspection, and verification should be run without cache to avoid stale typecheck or build artifacts.

CI runs Node 20.11.1 with pnpm 8.15.6 on ubuntu-latest. Core dep is zod 3.23.8 upgrading to 4.0.0-beta.4. Affected manifests: libs/core/package.json, services/billing/package.json, services/user/package.json. E2E env has NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules and DATABASE_URL=postgres://localhost:5432/test. Please reproduce with pnpm -r --filter ./services/* test.

Progress so far: I swept services/*/package.json and pinned core@^2.0.0; services/api-gateway/package.json:12 and services/billing/package.json:8 now declare core 2.x, while services/legacy-reporting/package.json:15 still has core 1.14.7. I ran pnpm -r list core and flagged 3 direct consumers plus 2 transitive overrides in pnpm-workspace.yaml:11. Typecheck shows breaking errors in services/api-gateway/src/client.ts:44 (initConfig signature changed) and services/billing/src/queue.ts:73 (EventBus constructor removed), so the public surface changed. Release tooling needs verification because .github/workflows/release.yml uses semantic-release per package and assumes lockfile integrity; pnpm-lock.yaml still has core 1.14.7 under overrides, and I have not checked whether independently released services require separate CHANGELOG bumps or independent tag patterns. Remaining unknown: whether core 2.x requires Node 20 across all services, whether legacy-reporting can be upgraded or needs an exception, and whether any downstream consumers outside this monorepo lock to core 1.x.

This fix is too narrow. Patching packages/core/src/client.ts for v9.0.0 while CORE_COMPAT_MODE=legacy hides the TypeError at Client.get (client.ts:214), but services/billing/src/sync.ts and services/search/src/query.ts still call the old fetchRecords() shape. Scratch the lockfile-drift theory. I bisected the failing `@acme/core` integration against the upgrade branch. The error is not caused by the 2.0.0 major bump’s ESM/CJS boundary or `exports` field. On `packages/core/package.json`, line 14, the `type: module` flag predates the bump, and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has `link-workspace-packages: false` unchanged since v1.9.4. I ran `pnpm why @acme/core --depth 1` in `services/user-api`, `services/billing`, and `services/search`: all resolve the exact 2.0.0 tarball hash `sha512-8f...`, no duplicated 1.13.2 copy. Also tested `--no-frozen-lockfile` in CI `upgrade-core-200.yml`, line 62; same `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` at `dist/index.js:37`. The previous suspect — mixed CJS consumers importing the new ESM entry — is ruled out because `services/billing` still uses CommonJS and passes when manually pointed to `@acme/core@1.13.2`, while `@acme/core@2.0.0` fails there identically. So the regression is introduced by the 2.0.0 dependency graph or its runtime contract, not workspace hoisting or package type misconfiguration.

This preserves independent releases because unchanged services continue to resolve the catalog version unless they opt into the new major through their own CI publish step.

After clearing the local store and rebuilding with --frozen-lockfile, the runtime error still occurs during bootstrap when the service loads core-plugin@1.4.0. So the failure is not caused by duplicated @acme/core copies or a stale hoisted dependency; it points toward initialization ordering or a changed export surface in 4.0.0, but I do not have enough evidence yet to identify the exact broken import.

The next file to inspect is pnpm-workspace.yaml, especially lines 1-18 for the packages: globs and any catalog: section that may centralize dependency versions. If the repo uses npm/yarn workspaces instead, I would pivot to the workspaces field near the top of package.json, but pnpm-workspace.yaml is the most likely place to discover the actual service package names and whether they share a common version block.
